scenes: Silo ships some classifiers.
You can add others: a script, a small model, or your own agent.
An added classifier is a program.
Nothing is loaded into Silo itself, so it runs in a computer of its own, with a boundary like any other.
It reads text that agents wrote: file names, commands, web pages.
That is how an agent could try to give it instructions.
Its boundary keeps that contained.
Letting it read a computer's record is a grant, and you make it.
Silo says the worst case first: this classifier can read everything recorded about main, and send it wherever its own network rules allow.
Silo shows that as a path, before you confirm.
What comes back is opinions, each pointing at the lines of the record that led to it.
It can also give panels for the app to draw, and questions for you.
It can never act on a computer, answer an ask, set or change a rule or a precaution, give a secret, or write into another computer.
What its opinion leads to is said by a precaution you set.
Classifiers work in three tiers.
Each wakes only when the one before cannot judge.
First the built-in classifiers.
They always run and cost no tokens.
Then a small model, for what they cannot judge.
Then an agent, which wakes when the small model is unsure, or when you ask it a question.
That third tier is the monitor agent you proposed: your own agent program, in its own computer.
Silo ships its recipe.
What an added classifier spends is your choice, and it is metered like any computer.
Pieces made by someone else arrive in a package, called a plugin: classifiers, rules and precautions, panels, and programs that forward alerts and asks to your phone.
Installing a plugin grants nothing.
Each rule, each precaution and each grant in it is shown to you, and you accept it or not.
In the older film a plugin could pause or stop a computer itself.
Not any more: it is only the package.
Before a classifier goes live, Silo can run it against the recorded past, in a fresh computer.
You see what it would have done: the opinions it would have given, and where it tried to connect.
How a piece is installed and started, and how you take a grant back, is not designed yet.
